title: Yet Trent lists hope and fiducia of divine mercy among dispositions to justification
source_text: XXXVIII. Nec tamen negant fiduciam illam unam esse ex conditionibus, sive dispositionibus ad justificationem necessariis & praerequisitis: ut videre est in ipso Concilio Tridentino, Sessione sexta, capite sexto, ubi inter dispositiones in adultis necessarias ad justitiam consequendam, spem & fiduciam divinae misericordiae collocat. Disponuntur autem, inquit, ad ipsam justitiam, dum excitati divina gratia & adjuti, fidem ex auditu concipientes, libere moventur in Deum, credentes vera esse quae divinitus revelata & promissa sunt, atque illud in primis, a Deo justificari impium per gratiam ejus, per redemptionem quae est in Christo Jesu: & dum peccatores se esse intelligentes, a divinae justitiae timore, quo utiliter concutiuntur, ad considerandam Dei misericordiam se convertendo, in spem eriguntur, fidentes Deum sibi propter Christum propitium fore, illumque tanquam omnis justitiae fontem diligere incipiunt.
pass_a_gloss: Yet they do not deny that that trust is one of the conditions or dispositions necessary and prerequisite for justification, as may be seen in the Council of Trent itself, Session six, chapter six, where among the dispositions necessary in adults for obtaining justice it places hope and trust of divine mercy. They are disposed to that justice itself, it says, when, stirred and helped by divine grace, conceiving faith from hearing, they are freely moved toward God, believing that what was divinely revealed and promised is true, and especially that God justifies the ungodly by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus; and when, understanding that they are sinners, from fear of divine justice by which they are usefully shaken, turning themselves to consider God mercy, they are raised to hope, trusting that God will be propitious to them on account of Christ, and they begin to love him as the fountain of all justice.
pass_b_english: Rome still counts that fiducia among the necessary prerequisite dispositions to justification; Trent sess. 6 c. 6 lists hope and trust of divine mercy among adult dispositions.

Trent sequence: grace-stirred hearing-faith, free movement to God, belief of revealed promises especially justification of the ungodly in Christ, salutary fear, turning to mercy, hope with trust God will be propitious for Christ sake, and beginning to love him as justice fountain.
